item.title: Generative artificial intelligence usage among graduate epidemiology students: a cross-sectional survey of use patterns, attitudes, and perceived learning gains
item.description: Purpose To characterize generative artificial intelligence (AI) use and attitudes among graduate epidemiology students and examine associations between AI attitudes, AI-use frequency, and self-reported perceived learning gains. Design/methodology/approach An anonymous cross-sectional survey was completed by 146 students enrolled in a required graduate epidemiology course across two cohorts. AI optimism was assessed using an adapted four-item AI Attitude Scale (AIAS-4), and perceived learning gains using the Student Assessment of their Learning Gains (SALG). Multinomial logistic and linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, language spoken at home, and cohort. Findings Of the 293 invited students, 146 participated (50%). AI use was infrequent for 25%, occasional for 40%, and frequent for 35%. Among 131 students with available helpfulness data, common uses included understanding concepts (79.4%), SAS programming (57.3%), and improving writing (42.0%). Higher AIAS-4 scores were associated with greater odds of occasional (OR = 2.24, 95% CI: 1.12–4.48) and frequent (OR = 9.18, 95% CI: 3.66–23.08) versus infrequent AI use. item.title: Digital readiness as an enabling capability for HyFlex-VR learning in vocational education
item.description: Purpose This study examines how perceived HyFlex-VR affordances and digital readiness relate to vocational students' learning experiences and whether readiness operates as a direct enabling capability or moderates the affordance–experience relationship. Design/methodology/approach A quantitatively dominant embedded mixed-method study involved 187 vocational high school students from South Sulawesi, Indonesia. After response quality screening, 169 cases were analysed using disjoint two-stage partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Digital readiness (digital infrastructure and competence) and learning experience (engagement and satisfaction) were modelled as formative higher-order composites. Open-ended survey responses were used to supplement the quantitative analysis. Findings Perceived HyFlex-VR affordances (ß = 0.216, p = 0.008) and digital readiness (ß = 0.584, p < 0.001) were positively associated with the learning experience (R2 = 0.529). item.title: The emotional labor of AI integration: a constructivist grounded theory study of academic librarians' work with generative AI tools
item.description: Purpose This study examines how academic librarians in Nigeria experience and manage emotional labor when they integrate generative artificial intelligence (AI) into reference services, and how that labor is carried out through epistemic work. Design/methodology/approach A constructivist grounded theory study was conducted in three academic libraries (federal, state and private) in Kwara State, Nigeria. Twenty-one reference, liaison and systems librarians took part through semi-structured interviews, non-participant observation of AI-mediated reference consultations and artifact analysis. Data were analyzed through initial and focused coding, constant comparison and memo writing. Findings Reference librarians' anxiety centered on professional credibility, liaison librarians' on bias in AI outputs and systems librarians' on technical instability. Librarians managed these feelings through two forms of epistemic work: epistemic vigilance, the alertness that sets how closely an output is checked, and epistemic stewardship, the verification and correction done to protect patrons. item.description: ABSTRACT Junior high school students frequently encounter obstacles in distinguishing poetry that conveys ideas literally from poetic works laden with symbolic expressions. This issue underpinned a quantitative investigation at SMP Negeri 2 Bawolato to empirically evaluate whether collaborative instruction through the Cooperative Learning model produces a measurable impact on eighth-grade students' proficiency in comparing diaphanous and prismatic poetry. Fifty students participated in a quasi-experimental study utilizing a pretest-posttest control group design, evenly distributed into an experimental group and a control group of 25 learners each. Learning achievement was measured using validated pre-test and post-test instruments and analyzed through prerequisite tests alongside an independent samples t-test at a 5% significance level. Data processing revealed that the experimental group's mean score rose from 49 to 80, whereas the control group increased from 47 to 76. item.title: Influence of Teachers’ Access to ICT Facilities on Students’ Academic Success in Public Secondary Schools in Nyamagana District, Tanzania
item.description: This study examined the influence of teachers’ access to Information and Communication Technology (ICT) facilities on students’ academic success in public secondary schools in Nyamagana District, Tanzania. The study was guided by the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) theory. The paper adopted a mixed-methods approach using a convergent parallel design. The target population comprised 53,463 respondents, from whom a sample of 201 participants was selected, including 100 students, 92 teachers, 5 heads of schools, 3 Ward Education Officers, and 1 District Secondary Education Officer. Data were collected using questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, and direct observation. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics with SPSS version 26, while qualitative data were analysed thematically. The findings revealed that teachers’ access to ICT facilities generally supported students’ academic success by improving their understanding of complex concepts, promoting engagement in learning activities, and supporting examination preparation. item.title: Applications of artificial intelligence in microbiology education
item.description: Microbiology underpins understanding of infectious disease, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), biotechnology, public health, food, agriculture and environmental sustainability. Although attention to artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has centred largely on generative tools, a broader range of AI technologies is creating opportunities across microbiology education. This article outlines applications in personalised learning, laboratory skills, diagnostics and image analysis, epidemiology and AMR education, drawing from contemporary literature. It distinguishes microbiology-specific evidence of educational benefit from professional exposure and evidence from other fields and suggests approaches educators can try. Potential benefits include engagement, conceptual understanding, accessibility and professional readiness, alongside challenges such as data privacy, digital inequity, environmental cost and overreliance on AI.

item.title: Associations Among AI Use, Learning Perception, and Character Perception in Madrasah Teachers: A Multi-Group SEM Study
item.description: How AI use relates to character-related judgments in madrasah education remains uncertain, particularly when learning and character are rated by the same teachers. This cross-sectional online survey analysed responses from 605 Indonesian madrasah teachers (RA–MI, n = 441; MTs–MA, n = 164) using confirmatory factor analysis and multi-group structural equation modelling. A correlated three-factor model (AI Use, Learning Perception, and Character Perception) fit better than simpler alternatives and met the tested measurement-invariance criteria. AI Use was positively associated with Learning Perception, and Learning Perception with Character Perception, whereas the direct AI Use–Character Perception paths were not statistically significant. Standardized indirect effects were 0.659 (95% bootstrap CI 0.560–0.767) for RA–MI and 0.696 (0.521–0.892) for MTs–MA. Their contrast was not statistically significant (standardized difference -0.037, CI -0.265 to 0.168), which does not establish group equivalence. item.title: Using Generative AI to Promote Mathematical Reasoning in Classrooms
STUDENT EXPERIENCE OF AI IN LAW ASSESSMENT: AN EXPLORATORY STUDY
item.description: Legal education faces particular challenges as a result of the wide dissemination of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI). GenAI can produce outputs that appear to challenge the work of licensed lawyers. This challenge requires educators and students to be knowledgeable about the powers and limitations of GenAI. This article presents a study of student experimentation with GenAI aimed at developing that knowledge. The experiment incorporated GenAI’s drafting capabilities into an assessment item required in a core subject, Tort Law. The article presents the responses and reflections of the students on the GenAI exercise and provokes further thinking about student experience, uses of and potential with GenAI in legal education. It argues that the most promising pedagogical response is neither blanket prohibition nor uncritical adoption, but a structured use-and-critique model in which students engage directly with GenAI and then evaluate its adequacy against disciplinary and professional standards.

item.description: Artificial intelligence is driving significant change in education in general with entrepreneurship included in this research. This research discusses how AI is making a difference in setting the entrepreneurial mindset of students. It explores how AI tools and platforms are increasingly reshaping the way of entrepreneurship is currently taught by providing personalized, interactive and hands-on learning experiences. Incorporating AI powered learning within the curriculum will inculcate an entrepreneurial mindset focusing on creativity, innovation and problem- solving. This research explores case studies of successful AI integration, in which these technologies further enhance the learning process in ultimately better to prepare students for a real-world entrepreneurial challenge. It is also discussed the benefits of AI in the personalization of education, mentorship and real time feedback. The challenges and ethical considerations for the use of AI in education are also explored and making sure that one gets full understanding and implications. item.title: AI readiness and indirect associations between AI literacy, TPB-based GAI antecedents, and behavioral intention to use generative AI among undergraduate nursing students: a cross-sectional study
item.description: Background Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into nursing education. Understanding factors associated with nursing students’ Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) use intention is essential. Aim This study examined the associations of AI literacy and TPB-based GAI antecedents with behavioral intention, and tested whether AI readiness was associated with the indirect pathways in two separate adjusted mediation models. Methods A cross-sectional survey of 650 undergraduate nursing students used the AI Literacy, AI Readiness, and GAI Behavior Influencing Factors scales. Results Mean scores were 64.71 ± 10.84 (AI literacy), 19.34 ± 2.46 (AI readiness), and 20.69 ± 3.68 (behavioral intention). In two separate adjusted mediation models, AI readiness was significantly associated with the indirect pathways from AI literacy (0.012, 95% CI: 0.005–0.020) and TPB-based GAI antecedents (0.013, 95% CI: 0.006–0.022), accounting for 37.5% and 4.2% of the total associations, respectively. item.title: Reciprocal within-person associations between physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment among primary school students participating in a cooperative games-based physical education curriculum: a four-wave random-intercept cross-lagged panel study
item.description: Introduction Physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment are central to children’s motivation to be active, yet their temporal ordering and within-person interplay remain unclear. This study examined their reciprocal associations among 1,279 Chinese students in Grades 5 and 6 participating in a cooperative games-based physical education curriculum. Methods General physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment were assessed on four occasions separated by 33, 28, and 28 days. Longitudinal measurement invariance was tested before conventional cross-lagged panel models and random-intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs) were compared. The primary RI-CLPM used class-clustered robust maximum likelihood and full information maximum likelihood for missing data. item.title: From Affordance to Coupling: Reconstructing Foreign Language Pedagogy through an AI-Enabled Production-Oriented Approach
item.description: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is now a routine presence in foreign language classrooms, yet the gap between what the technology can do and what it actually teaches remains poorly theorised. This paper argues that the gap is structural, and that it is best analysed at the level of the pedagogic move. Taking the Production-Oriented Approach (POA) as its anchor, the paper identifies three chronic constraints in POA practice: the cost of evaluating student output, the difficulty of matching input to diagnosed gaps, and the delay between production and feedback. It then proposes the construct of an AI-enabled Production-Oriented Approach (AI-POA), which frames AI as a change in the resourcing and pacing of an existing cycle. Three affordances of generative AI (generative, dialogic, evaluative) are specified, together with four conditions under which they couple with instruction: goal alignment, temporal placement, cognitive appropriateness and teacher control. A nine-move cycle is derived, and implications for objectives, materials, assessment, teacher judgement and institutional arrangements are discussed. item.title: Internalizing Love-Based Curriculum Values in Akidah Akhlak Learning: Strategies and Challenges in Madrasah
item.description: This study aims to analyze the strategies used in internalizing Love-Based Curriculum values in Akidah Akhlak learning at MTs Cijawura Kota Bandung. A qualitative case study design was employed involving one Akidah Akhlak teacher, one madrasah leader, and five students from Grades VII and VIII. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, observation, and documentation and analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing or verification. The findings show that Love-Based Curriculum values were internalized through integrated pedagogical strategies combining value-based lesson planning, differentiated and joyful learning, dialogical interaction, teacher role modeling, habituation, reflection, and behavioral observation. The internalized values covered spiritual, personal, social, intellectual, environmental, and national dimensions. The process was strengthened by institutional support, religious habituation, positive madrasah culture, teacher exemplarity, and student participation. item.title: Addressing the Youth Suicide Crisis: Policy Recommendations for Schools, Communities, and Health Care Settings
item.description: About 10% of high school students reported a suicide attempt in 2023, indicating that growing youth suicide rates are an emerging public health crisis. Social and structural factors including trauma, marginalization, and systemic racism contribute to disparities in youth suicide risk and underscore the need to prioritize culturally relevant and responsive crisis intervention. We promote four policy recommendations: (a) placing 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, Crisis Text Line, and local resources on all high school and college student IDs; (b) expanding state-sponsored community and school programs; (c) implementing universal school-based mental health screenings; and (d) promoting lethal means restriction. These policies address critical gaps in current youth suicide prevention approaches.

item.description: 21st-century education demands a learning approach that develops not only academic achievement but also meaningfulness, awareness, and joy toward diverse student needs. However, previous research tends to separate differentiated learning, game-based learning, and formative assessment, leaving few models that simultaneously optimize cognitive and affective dimensions. This study evaluates the DIGA-FAM (Differentiated Instruction and Game-Based Formative Assessment) model to foster mindfulness, meaningfulness, and joyfulness through interactive Wordwall in poetry text learning. Using a descriptive research design, student perceptions and classroom responses were collected from a single sample of 48 students at SMK Negeri 3 Padang through a validated Likert-scale questionnaire and classroom observation, complemented by one teacher's perspective via semi-structured interview, then triangulated for comprehensive interpretation. item.title: Development of Web-Based Learning Media for Teaching Trigonometric Ratios to Grade X Students
item.description: Teaching trigonometric ratios remains challenging because students often struggle with abstract concepts, conventional instruction predominates, and digital learning resources are underused. This study developed a Google Sites learning resource for teaching trigonometric ratios to tenth-grade students at MAS TI Batang Kabung and evaluated its validity and practicality. The study followed the 4D development model (Define, Design, Develop, and Disseminate) and involved one mathematics teacher and 25 tenth-grade students in a product trial. Data were collected through observations, interviews, documentation, and validation and practicality questionnaires, then analyzed using descriptive quantitative and qualitative techniques. Expert validation scores for content and media were 91.07% and 92.11%, respectively, both classified as highly valid. Practicality scores were 93.42% from the teacher and 86.26% from the students, yielding an overall mean of 89.84%, classified as highly practical. The resource brings together instructional materials, illustrations, videos, exercises, and assessments on a single website. item.title: Design of a Personalized Learning System for Higher Education Using Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Mobile Technologies
item.description: Mobile learning in higher education is shifting from ubiquitous access toward contextsensitive personalization. However, cloud-based recommendation systems are constrained by unpredictable latency, insufficient contextual awareness, and limited capacity for continuous adaptation. To address these limitations, an on-device context-adaptive personalization loop (OCAPL) was proposed, in which personalized inference, path generation, and online adaptation were performed directly on mobile devices. The proposed framework was built on three technical pillars: on-device multimodal state inference, context-constrained path generation, and implicit-feedback-driven parameter-efficient updating. Learning behaviors, touch interactions, and device context were jointly integrated. Learning actions were subsequently generated under constraints on latency, energy consumption, memory, and path coherence. Continuous adaptation was further enabled by natural interaction signals and low-rank fine-tuning. Experimental results demonstrate that OCAPL maintained on-device inference latency below 200 ms, peak memory usage below 50 MB, and additional energy consumption below 5% per hour of learning. item.title: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF EUROPEAN AND UKRAINIAN FRAMEWORKS GOVERNING THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN RESEARCH AND EDUCATION
item.description: This article presents a comparative analysis of the principal policy and regulatory documents governing the use of generative artificial intelligence in research and higher education. The study examines the European Living Guidelines (third edition, May 2026), the Ukrainian recommendations on the use of artificial intelligence in research (October 2026), and the Ukrainian recommendations for higher education institutions (April 2025). It considers the circumstances that prompted these documents in the context of the emerging concept of postplagiarism, the adoption of Ukraine’s Law on Academic Integrity, and the implementation of the European Union’s Artificial Intelligence Act. Using a framework developed for this study and comprising six categories of comparative indicators, the analysis compares the documents’ legal status, target audiences, classifications of AI use and risk assessment criteria, integrity standards and disclosure mechanisms based on the GAIDeT taxonomy, restrictions on the use of AI detection tools, and models of institutional governance. Detailed practical examples illustrate how these frameworks can be implemented in research and education.

item.title: AI-Powered Attention Monitoring with Live Computer Vision Processing
item.description: Abstract In fields like driver safety, remote work, online education, and cognitive evaluation, real-time attention monitoring is becoming more and more necessary. Existing solutions typically rely on cloud-based APIs, specialized sensors, or heavyweight native applications, which restrict accessibility, scalability, and privacy. Using MediaPipe Face Landmarker and TensorFlow.js for real-time computer vision processing, this paper introduces a fully browser-based, AI-powered attention monitoring system. Using JavaScript and Web APIs, the suggested system operates fully on the client side. It processes offline and live webcam footage, extracts facial landmarks, eye aspect ratio (EAR), head pose proxies, and gaze direction, and calculates an interpretable attention score for each frame. Real-time charts, blink-rate estimation, head-movement indicators, configurable thresholds, distraction alerts, and comprehensive post-session analytics are all included in the application's rich dashboard.
